Last night, I stayed up until 3 a.m. just trying to figure out what to say to my friend when she broke down again. I kept thinking, “If I just said the right thing, everything would change,” but then I realized I didn’t even know what that was. And when I finally went to sleep, I woke up and couldn’t remember my own name. It felt like I was just going in circles—trying to fix something that wasn’t broken, and not even sure if I was helping or just making it worse.

I remember one night when I was sitting on the couch, just staring at the floor, and my friend said, “I don’t know if I can go on.” I didn’t say anything at first—just looked at her, like I was waiting for the right thing to come. But then I started thinking about all the times I’ve tried to fix things, and I realized I wasn’t even sure what I was supposed to feel. I just kept trying to fix it, like if I showed up, if I listened, if I said something kind, it would magically change. But when I looked at my hands, I didn’t recognize them. Like I was watching someone else’s life through my own eyes. And that’s when I knew—I wasn’t helping her. I was just trying to save myself from the feeling of being helpless. And that felt worse than anything.

I think I started losing myself the first time I realized I wasn’t even angry at her for being sad—because I used to think if I was angry, I was doing something right. But now I just feel empty. Like every time I try to help, I’m not really helping at all. I’m just filling the silence with words that don’t mean anything. And when I look at myself in the mirror now, I don’t see someone who cares—I see someone who’s been trying too hard to fix things that can’t be fixed. It’s like I’ve forgotten how to just be. And that’s when I know—I’m not helping her. I’m just keeping her pain alive in my own chest.

I don’t know if I’m even supposed to be here anymore. I used to think showing up was enough—just being present, just listening. But now I feel like I’m not even present to myself. Every time I try to breathe, it feels like I’m holding my breath for her. And when I finally let go, I realize I didn’t feel anything—no anger, no relief, no hope. Just this heavy quiet, like I’ve been drowning in the same water for so long that I don’t know what it feels like to float. Is that what it means to lose yourself? To stop knowing who you are, just because you keep trying to fix what’s broken?
